body.text:
asti śrīmati+akhilavasudhāsundare candanādrau
gandharvāṇām+kanakanagarī nāma ramyas+nivāsas+|
haimais+līlābhavanaśikharais+ambaram+vyālikhadbhis+
dhatte śākhānagaragaṇanām+yas+surāṇām+purasya|| 1
body.translated_text: On the glorious Sandal Mountain (<s>Candanādri</s>), the most beautiful [mountain] in all the earth, there is a delightful abode of the <s>Gandharvas</s> called the Golden City (<s>Kanakanagarī</s>), whose golden pinnacles of pleasure-palaces scratch the sky — it holds the reputation of being [counted as] a city among the branch-cities of the gods. // 1

body.text:
tasmin+ekā kuvalayavatī nāma gandharvakanyā
manye jaitram+mṛdu kusumatas+api+āyudham+yā smarasya|
dṛṣṭvā devam+bhuvanavijaye lakṣmaṇam+kṣoṇipālam+
bālā sadyas+kusumadhanuṣas+saṃvidheyībabhūva|| 2
body.translated_text: In that [city] there was a <s>Gandharva</s> maiden named <s>Kuvalayavatī</s>, who, I think, was the victorious weapon of <s>Smara</s> (the god of love), softer even than flowers. Having seen the king <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> during the conquest of the worlds, the young girl immediately became subject to the flower-bowed [god of love]. // 2

body.text:
bālyeṣu+ālīṣu+api manasijam+sā+anabhivyañjayantī
pāṇḍukṣāmā katicit+anayat+kātarā vāsarāṇi|
gantum+deśāntaram+atha madhau+anyathā+eva pravṛttam+
gāḍhotkaṇṭhā malayapavanam+sapraṇāmam+yayāce|| 3
body.translated_text: Not revealing her passion even to her young companions, she spent several days pale and emaciated, anxious. But when in the spring season [her beloved] set out for another land, overwhelmed by intense longing, she respectfully implored the <s>Malaya</s> breeze: // 3

body.text:
tvattas+prāṇās+sakalajagatām+dakṣiṇas+tvam+prakṛtyā
jaṅghālam+tvām+pavana manasas+anantaram+vyāharanti|
tasmāt+eva tvayi khalu mayā sampraṇītas+arthibhāvas+
prāyas+bhikṣā bhavati viphalā na+eva yuṣmadvidheṣu|| 4
body.translated_text: "From you come the life-breaths of all beings; you are by nature compassionate. They call you, O wind, the swiftest after the mind. Therefore it is in you that I have placed my suppliant hopes — for a petition is generally never fruitless before those such as you. // 4

body.text:
vīkṣya+avasthām+virahavidhurām+rāmacandrasya hetos+
yātas+pāram+pavana saritām+patyus+api+āñjaneyas+|
tat+tātasya+apratihatagates+yāsyatas+te madartham+
gauḍī kṣoṇī kati nu malayakṣmādharāt+yojanāni|| 5
body.translated_text: Having seen the love-stricken condition [of <s>Sītā</s>], for the sake of <s>Rāmacandra</s>, <s>Āñjaneya</s> (<s>Hanumān</s>), the son of the wind (<s>Pavana</s>), crossed to the other side of the ocean. So for you, son of that father of unobstructed course, who will go on my behalf — how many <s>yojanas</s> is the land of <s>Gauḍa</s> from the <s>Malaya</s> mountain? // 5

body.text:
tatra+avaśyam+kusumasamaye sa tvayā śīlanīyas+
sāndrodyānasthagitagaganaprāṅgaṇas+gauḍadeśas+|
tat+me+avasthām+kathaya nṛpates+jīvanatrāṇahetos+
prādurbhāvas+trijagati khalu tvādṛśānām+parārthas+|| 6
body.translated_text: There you must certainly frequent, in the season of flowers, the land of <s>Gauḍa</s>, whose dense gardens obscure the horizon of the sky. So tell the king of my condition, for the sake of preserving my life — for the appearance of those such as you in the three worlds is indeed for the benefit of others. // 6

body.text:
hṛtvā+anarghyam+parimalam+itas+candanānokahānām+
tūrṇam+tāvat+visṛja malayopatyakākānanāni|
yāvat+na+ete nidhuvanakalākelibhājas+bhujaṅgās+
bhogavyājāt+culukaculukam+matsarās+tvām+pibanti|| 7
body.translated_text: Having carried away the priceless fragrance from the sandal trees here, quickly leave the forests on the slopes of the <s>Malaya</s> [mountain] — before these serpents, who partake of the art of love-play, jealously drink you up sip by sip under the pretext of [spreading] their hoods. // 7

body.text:
śrīkhaṇḍādres+parisaram+atikramya gavyūtimātram+
gantavyas+te kim+api jagatīmaṇḍanam+pāṇḍyadeśas+|
tatra khyātam+puram+uragam+iti+ākhyayā tāmrapārṇyās+
tīre mugdhakramukatarubhis+baddharekhe bhajethās+|| 8
body.translated_text: Having crossed beyond the environs of the <s>Śrīkhaṇḍa</s> mountain by a mere <s>gavyūti</s> (league), you must travel to the <s>Pāṇḍya</s> country, an ornament of the world. There you should resort to the famous city called by the name '<s>Uraga</s>' (Serpent City), on the banks of the <s>Tāmraparṇī</s>, bordered by rows of innocent areca-nut trees. // 8

body.text:
sambhogānte ślathabhujalatāniḥsahānām+vadhūnām+
vyādhunvantas+anucitakavarībhāram+avyājamugdham|
asmin+sadyas+śramajalanudas+saudhajālais+upetya
pratyāsannās+malayamarutas+tālavṛntībhavanti|| 9
body.translated_text: At the end of lovemaking, the <s>Malaya</s> breezes, dispelling fatigue, approaching through the latticed windows of the mansions, instantly blow upon the disheveled and artlessly charming hair of the young women whose vine-like arms have loosened in exhaustion — and become [like] palm-leaf fans (<s>tālavṛntī</s>). // 9

body.text:
krīḍāśailam+bhujaganagarīyoṣitām+kautukam+cet+
setum+yāyās+jaladhikariṇas+śṛṅkhalādāma dīrgham|
bhāti snehāt+avanitanayājīvanāśvāsahetos+
laṅkādvīpam+prahitas+iva yas+bāhus+ekas+pṛthivyās+|| 10
body.translated_text: If you have the curiosity to see the pleasure-mountain of the women of the Serpent City, you should go to the bridge (<s>setu</s>) — the long chain-garland of the ocean-elephant. It shines forth, as if out of affection, like a single arm of the earth extended for the sake of reassuring and reviving the daughter of the earth (<s>Sītā</s>), [reaching toward] the island of <s>Laṅkā</s>. // 10

body.text:
krudhyadgaurīkarakiśalayākṛṣṭacūḍāsudhāṃśos+
drakṣyasi+uccais+kulam+akaluṣam+tatra rāmeśvarasya|
madhyam+yatra trivaliviṣamam+vārasīmantinīnām+
hastotkampam+kathayati vidhes+sṛṣṭakāñcīpadasya|| 11
body.translated_text: There you will see from above the spotless lineage of <s>Rāmeśvara</s>, [the temple of] <s>Śiva</s> whose crescent-moon-crest is pulled by the playful shoot-like hand of angry <s>Gaurī</s> — the place where the trembling hands of the ocean-bordering women, with their waists uneven with three folds, speak of the creator's hand-tremor when he fashioned their girdle-ornaments. // 11

body.text:
līlāgārais+amaranagarasya+api garvam+harantīm+
gacches+kāñcīpuram+atha diśas+bhūṣaṇam+dakṣiṇasyās+|
naktam+yatra praharikas+iva+ujjāgaram+nāgarāṇām+
kurvan+pāṇipraṇihitadhanus+jāyate pañcabāṇas+|| 12
body.translated_text: Then proceed to <s>Kāñcīpuram</s>, the ornament of the southern direction, which surpasses even the city of the gods with its pleasure-palaces. Where at night the five-arrowed one [<s>Kāma</s>, the god of love], holding a bow placed in his hand, becomes like a night-watchman, keeping the citizens awake. // 12

body.text:
ābhram+līlāvihasitam+iva śyāvatām+abhyupete
sadyas+phenavyatikaramiṣādarpayati+aṃśukāntam(?)|
ambhaḥkrīḍākutukarabhasabhraṣṭacīnottarīye
yannārīṇām+urasi subalā vīcihastais+sakhī+iva|| 13
body.translated_text: When the dark river (<s>Kāverī</s>) assumes [the appearance of] a cloud — as if playfully laughing — she instantly adorns the hem of the garments [of the bathing women] under the pretext of mingling foam. [She], like a strong and intimate friend, [plays] with wave-hands upon the bosoms of the women whose Chinese silk upper garments have slipped off in the eagerness of water-sport. // 13

body.text:
manye mokṣas+kaṭhinasuratāyāsalabdhasya tūrṇam+
duṣprāpas+te pavana bhavitā colasīmantinībhyas+|
ke vā tāsām+alakaracanālīnanīlīsanāthe
gaṇḍābhoge malayajapayaḥpicchile na skhalanti|| 14
body.translated_text: I think, O wind, liberation from the <s>Cola</s> women, from whom hard-won relief after the exertion of fierce lovemaking [has been obtained], will be difficult for you to attain quickly. For who does not stumble upon their cheek-slopes, slippery with sandal-paste water, and adorned with blue <s>nīlī</s> (indigo) nestled in their hair-arrangements? // 14

body.text:
hitvā kāñcīm+avinayavatībhaktarodhonikuñjām+
tām+kāverīm+anusara khagaśreṇivācālakūlām|
kāntāśleṣāt+api khalu sukhasparśam+indutviṣas+api
svaccham+bhikṣāpravaṇamanasas+api+ambu yasyās+laghīyas+|| 15
body.translated_text: Leaving <s>Kāñcī</s>, with its bower-arbors beloved of immodest women, follow that <s>Kāverī</s> river, whose banks are made noisy by rows of birds. Her water is pleasanter to the touch than even a lover's embrace, cooler than moonlight, transparent, and lighter than even [the water given as] alms to one whose mind is inclined toward begging. // 15

body.text:
yā gaṅgā+iva prakṛtisubhagā jāyate keralīnām+
kelisnāne kucamalayajais+pāṇḍimānam+dadhānā|
śaśvadgotraskhalanajanitatrāsalolasya sindhos+
udvīcibhrus+caraṇapatanapremavācām+rasajñā|| 16
body.translated_text: She who, like the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, is naturally beautiful among the <s>Kerala</s> women, assuming whiteness from the sandal paste of Malaya [smeared on her] breasts during playful bathing, wise in the language of love [spoken by] the waves' eyebrow-like crests of the ocean, which trembles with fear born of the constant crumbling of its banks. || 16

body.text:
tasyās+līlāsaritas+iva tās+srotasi śroṇidaghne
toyakrīḍām+yadi vidadhate dākṣiṇātyās+taruṇyas+|
vīcikṣepais+stanaparisareṣu+astahāreṣu tāsām+
muktājālam+racaya tat+apām+bindubhis+kundagaurais+|| 17
body.translated_text: If those southern young women engage in water-play in the current of her sport-rivers, breast-deep, with the sashes on the regions of their breasts loosened by the splashing of waves, then fashion for them a net of pearls with drops of water white as jasmine. || 17

body.text:
snigdhaśyāmam+gurubhis+upalais+parvatam+mālyavantam+
paśyes+uttambhitam+iva puras+keśapāśam+pṛthivyās+|
tatra+adya+api pratijharajalais+jarjarās+prasthabhāgās+
sītābhartus+pṛthutaraśucas+sūcayanti+aśrupātān|| 18
body.translated_text: You shall behold Mount <s>Mālyavat</s>, dark and lustrous with massive rocks, raised up before you like the tress of hair of the Earth; where even today the slopes, battered by the waters of every cascade, reveal the copious tears of <s>Sītā</s>'s lord [<s>Rāma</s>]. || 18

body.text:
ramyopāntam+saralatarubhis+māṇḍakarṇas+saras+tat+
gacches+pañcāpsaras+iti hṛtaprauḍhatāpam+maghonas+|
yatra+adya+api tridaśataruṇīmugdhasaṃgītimālā
pūrvapremopagatahariṇaśreṇim+utkaṇṭhayanti|| 19
body.translated_text: Go to that lake <s>Māṇḍakarṇa</s>, also called <s>Pañcāpsaras</s> (Five Apsarases), lovely with <s>sarala</s> (pine) trees at its edges, which has removed the intense heat of <s>Indra</s> (<s>Maghona</s>); where even today the garlands of song of the innocent celestial maidens fill with longing the herds of deer who had experienced love in the past. || 19

body.text:
krīḍāśokakramukabahulārāmaramyopakaṇṭhās+
sampatsyante pathi pathi tava prītaye prasthitasya|
pīnottuṅgastanabharanamatpāmarīpremalobhāt+
nirvicchedabhramitapathikās+pallayas+palvalinyas+|| 20
body.translated_text: Beautiful in their outskirts with pleasure-gardens rich in <s>aśoka</s> and <s>kramuka</s> (areca) trees, there will appear on every road, to delight you as you proceed, villages (<s>palvalīs</s>) whose roads are ceaselessly traversed by travelers tempted by love for low-caste women bowed under the weight of their plump, lofty breasts. || 20

body.text:
andhrān+hitvā janapadavadhūgāḍhagodāvarīkān+
kāliṅgasya+anusara nagarīm+nāma tām+rājadhānīm|
sambhogānte mukulitadṛśām+tatra vārāṅganānām+
aṅgaglānim+hara paripatan+kelivātāyaneṣu|| 21
body.translated_text: Leaving the <s>Andhra</s> country, whose women are deeply attached to the <s>Godāvarī</s>, follow the kingdom of <s>Kāliṅga</s> to that city called the Royal Capital; there, at the end of lovemaking, gliding through their pleasure-windows, relieve the languor of the limbs of the courtesans whose eyes are half-closed. || 21

body.text:
kheladvīcipracayaracitānekasopānarekham+
tīram+yāyās+phalabharanamatpūgamālam+payodhes+|
gāyantīnām+śravaṇasubhagam+tatra siddhāṅganānām+
sthāne sthāne janaya śanakais+tān+aśabdānuvādān|| 22
body.translated_text: Go to the shore of the ocean, [its banks] bearing the appearance of many stairways formed by rows of playful waves, [its shore] with areca-palm garlands bending under the weight of fruit; and there, gently produce those soundless echoes of the songs of the <s>Siddha</s> women, pleasing to the ear, at every spot. || 22

body.text:
kuñjakrīḍattridaśataruṇīkeliniśvāsavātais+
glāyadvallīkiśalayarucas+nirviśes+vindhyapādān|
paśyan+vaktrāṇi+anaticaturavyādhasīmantinīnām+
mādyadgandhadviradarasitatrāsalolekṣaṇāni|| 23
body.translated_text: Enter the foothills of the <s>Vindhya</s>, where the radiance of tender vine-shoots fades in the breezes — the sighing breaths of celestial maidens sporting in the bowers — beholding the faces of the not-overly-clever woodland women, their eyes trembling with alarm at the scent of maddened rutting elephants. || 23

body.text:
svecchāramyam+vihara vihagavyākulottuṅgavṛkṣe
vindhotsaṅgapraṇayini vane mānavatyas+api yatra|
saṃjāyante rahasi kariṇām+krūram+ākarṇya śabdam+
bhartus+kaṇṭhe praṇihitabhujāvallayas+bhillayoṣās+|| 24
body.translated_text: Wander at your pleasure in the forest on the lap of the <s>Vindhya</s>, dear [to you], where the trees are tall and bustling with birds; where <s>Bhilla</s> women, hearing the fierce sound of elephants in the forest, become creepers clasping their husbands' necks with their arms. || 24

body.text:
svairakrīḍārasikaśabarīsiktarodhonikuñjām+
gacches+revām+abhinavaśukaśyāmavaṃśīvanena|
manyante yat+parisarabhuvi prauḍhasīmantinīnām+
līlāmānagraham+api rates+antarāyam+yuvānas+|| 25
body.translated_text: Go to the <s>Revā</s> (Narmadā) river, whose bank-thickets are sprinkled by <s>Śabarī</s> women at play, with its bamboo groves dark as fresh parrots; near whose banks, young men consider even the playful pretense of anger by mature women as an obstacle to lovemaking. || 25

body.text:
līlām+netum+nayanapadavīm+keralīnām+rates+cet+
gacches+khyātām+jagati nagarīm+ākhyayā tām+yayātes+|
gāḍhāśliṣṭakramukataravas+prāṅgaṇe nāgavallyas+
bālām+yatra priyatamaparīrambham+adhyāpayanti|| 26
body.translated_text: If you wish to bring the beauty of <s>Kerala</s> women into the sight of the eyes, go to that city renowned in the world by the name of <s>Yayāti</s>; where in the courtyards, betel-vines (<s>nāgavallī</s>) tightly embracing areca trees teach young girls the embrace of a beloved. || 26

body.text:
gaṅgāvīciplutaparisaras+saudhamālāvataṃsas+
yāsyati+uccais+tvayi rasamayas+vismayam+suhmadeśas+|
śrotrakrīḍābharaṇapadavīm+bhūmidevāṅganānām+
tālīpatram+navaśaśikalākomalam+yatra yāti|| 27
body.translated_text: The land of <s>Suhma</s>, adorned with a garland of mansions, its environs flooded by waves of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, will rise up to inspire wonder in you as you, full of delight [pass by]; where the palm-leaf manuscripts, soft as the new crescent moon, travel the path of ornamental delight for the ears of the wives of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. || 27

body.text:
tasmin+senānvayanṛpatinā devarājyābhiṣiktas+
devas+suhme vasati kamalākelikāras+murāris+|
pāṇau līlākamalam+asakṛt+yatsamīpe vahantyas+
lakṣmīśaṅkām+prakṛtisubhagās+kurvate vārarāmās+|| 28
body.translated_text: In that <s>Suhma</s> land dwells the god <s>Murāri</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), the sport of <s>Lakṣmī</s>, consecrated as divine king by that lord of armies descended from the <s>Sena</s> lineage; in whose vicinity, naturally beautiful courtesans, repeatedly bearing a playful lotus in hand, arouse the suspicion of being <s>Lakṣmī</s> herself. || 28

body.text:
yātasya+ūrdhvam+dhanapatiganena+eva gaurais+agārais+
paśyes+tasmin+nagaram+anagham+cāru candrārdhamaules+|
yatra+anekapriyanakhapadavyājatas+vārarāmās+
bhartus+bhūṣāśaśadharakalācihnam+aṅke vahanti|| 29
body.translated_text: Having gone further on the path of the lord of wealth [<s>Kubera</s>, i.e., northward], you shall see in that [land] the faultless, beautiful city of the one who wears the crescent moon [<s>Śiva</s>], with its white houses; where courtesans bear on their bodies the mark of the moon-crescent — [which is actually] the imprint of their beloved's nails in the guise of many lover's nail-marks. || 29

body.text:
tatra+anarghyam+raghukulagurum+svarṇadītīradeśe
natvā devam+vraja girisutāsaṃvibhaktāṅgaramyam|
yāte yasmin+nayanapadavīm+sundarabhrūlatānām+
prauḍhastrīṇām+galati ramaṇapremajanmābhimānas+|| 30
body.translated_text: There, bowing to the priceless god, the preceptor of the <s>Raghu</s> dynasty, at the bank of the river <s>Svarṇadī</s> (Golden River), go to the one who is lovely in form shared with the daughter of the mountain (<s>Girisutā</s>, i.e., <s>Pārvatī</s>); upon whose departure from the sight of mature women's beautiful eyebrow-creepers, the pride born of their husbands' love fades away. || 30

body.text:
tat+kṣetram+ca tridivasaritam+ca+antarā sevanīyas+
śrīballālakṣitipatiyaśobāndhavas+setubandhas+|
ārūḍhānām+tridivataṭinīsnānahetos+janānām+
yatra dvedhā+api+amaranagarī sannikṛṣṭā vibhāti|| 31
body.translated_text: Between that land and the celestial river (<s>Gaṅgā</s>), you should visit the bridge — the kinsman of the fame of King <s>Śrī Ballāla</s> — where, for people who have ascended to bathe in the celestial river, the city of the gods appears nearby in twofold [reflected] splendor. || 31 ||

body.text:
gaṅgām+phenastabakamukuram+vīcihaste vahantīm+
sevethās+tām+atha parisaraprauḍhahaṃsāvataṃsām|
pratyāvṛtya vrajati jaladhau preyasi premalolā
kartum+keśagraham+iva kim+api+uddhatā yā vibhāti|| 32
body.translated_text: Then attend upon the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, who carries in her wave-hands a mirror of foam-clusters, adorned with full-grown swans upon her banks; she who, loving and restless, turns back and flows into the ocean, appears raised up as if to seize [her beloved's] hair. || 32 ||

body.text:
toyakrīḍāsarasanipatatsuhmasīmantinīnām+
vīcīdhautais+stanamṛgamadas+śyāmalībhūya bhūyas+|
bhāgīrathyās+tapanatanayā yatra niryāti devī
deśam+yāyās+tam+atha jagatīpāvanam+bhaktinamras+|| 33
body.translated_text: Where the musk on the breasts of women plunging eagerly into water-play, washed by the waves, grows dark once more — there the divine <s>Bhāgīrathī</s> (Gaṅgā, daughter of <s>Bhagīratha</s>) and the daughter of the Sun (<s>Yamunā</s>) emerge. Then, bowing with devotion, go to that land that purifies the earth. || 33 ||

body.text:
saṃsarpantīm+prakṛtikuṭilām+darśitāvartacakrām+
tām+ālokya tridaśasaritas+nirgatām+ambugarbhāt|
mā nirmuktāsitaphaṇivadhūśaṅkayā kātaras+bhūs+
bhītas+sarvas+bhavati bhujagāt+kim+punas+tvādṛśas+yas+|| 34
body.translated_text: Seeing the celestial river emerging from the depths of the water, naturally crooked, displaying circles of whirlpools — do not be frightened with the suspicion that it is a released dark cobra-bride; everyone is afraid of serpents — how much more so one like you! || 34 ||

body.text:
krīḍantīnām+payasi rabhasāt+tatra līlāvatīnām+
vīcīhastais+racaya kucayos+aṃśukasraṃsanāni|
sadyas+tāsām+api ca ramaṇālokanavyākulānām+
yāntu krīḍāmasṛṇahasitāni+uttarīyāñcalatvam|| 35
body.translated_text: Of women playing vigorously in the water there with grace — with wave-hands, arrange the loosening of garments from their breasts; and immediately, of those women too, agitated at the sight of their lovers, let their smiles, soft from play, serve as the edges of their upper garments. || 35 ||

body.text:
skandhāvāram+vijayapuram+iti+unnatām+rājadhānīm+
dṛṣṭvā tāvat+bhuvanajayinas+tasya rājñas+adhigacches+|
gaṅgāvātas+tvam+iva caturas+yatra paurāṅganānām+
sambhogānte sapadi vtanoti+aṅgasaṃvāhanāni|| 36
body.translated_text: Having seen the lofty capital called <s>Vijayapura</s> (City of Victory), the military encampment of that world-conquering king, you should arrive there; where the <s>Gaṅgā</s>-breeze, clever like you, immediately after lovemaking performs body-massages for the city women. || 36 ||

body.text:
yatsadhānām+upari vaḍabhīśālabhañjīṣu līnās+
susnigdhāsu prakṛtimadhurās+kelikautūhalena|
unnīyante katham+api rahaḥpāṇipaṅkeruhāgrasparśodgacchatpulakamukulās+subhruvas+vallabhena|| 37
body.translated_text: Where upon the balcony-railings of the houses of the virtuous, sheltering in the smooth lattice-windows, naturally sweet [women], with playful curiosity, are somehow raised up in private by the lover, their limbs sprouting goosebumps like buds from the touch of lotus-like fingertips. || 37 ||

body.text:
snigdhaśyāmāramaṇamaṇibhis+baddhamundhālavālās+
paurastrībhis+kramukataravas+ropitās+prāṅgaṇeṣu|
yatra+ayatnopagatasalilais+naktam+āsiktamūlās+
na+apekṣante parijanavadhūpāṇiviśrāṇitāmbhas+|| 38
body.translated_text: Where areca-nut trees planted in courtyards by city women, with bases bound by beautiful dark ornamental gems, their roots irrigated at night by water that comes effortlessly, do not require water dispensed by the hands of maidservants. || 38 ||

body.text:
gaṅgāśleṣaprakṛtivimale pālite tena rājñā
jātā lokadvitayavigaladbhītayas+yatra paurās+|
bālābhyas+atha praṇayakalahais+rūḍhakopāṅkurābhyas+
vicasyanti bhrukuṭiracanācārubhīmānanābhyas+|| 39
body.translated_text: In [the city] protected by that king, naturally pure from the embrace of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, the citizens have become free from the fears of both worlds; but from young women in whom sprouts of anger have grown through lovers' quarrels, they shrink back from their beautifully fearsome faces adorned with knitted brows. || 39 ||

body.text:
āttam+karṇāt+praṇihitapadam+sāñjanais+aśruleśais+
baddham+tāpaglapitabisinītantunā bandhanena|
yatra strīṇām+adhararucakanyastasindūramudram+
tālīpatram+praṇayini jane premalekhatvam+eti|| 40
body.translated_text: Where the palm-leaf [letter], taken from the ear, placed at the feet, marked with drops of tears mixed with collyrium, bound with a string of lotus-stalk wilted by the heat [of passion], stamped with a vermilion seal pressed upon the lip-ornament — becomes a love-letter to the affectionate lover. || 40 ||

body.text:
bhartus+svairam+suratajanitasvedabindūn+vinetum+
yatra snehāt+agaṇitajinaglānibhis+mugdhadārais+|
sīdhotsaṅge śaśadhararucas+tantujālapraviṣṭās+
vyākṛṣyante ruciracamarībālabhārabhrameṇa|| 41
body.translated_text: Where, in order to freely wipe away the beads of sweat produced by lovemaking on the husband's [body], by innocent wives with unstinting and loving weariness — threads of beautiful yak-tail fans, white as moonbeams, having entered through the latticed nets over the wine-cup, are drawn out with the semblance of pulling the weight of fine <s>cāmarī</s> (yak-tail) hair. || 41 ||

body.text:
vṛddhoṣmāṇas+stanaparisarās+kuṅkumasya+aṅgarāgās+
dolās+kelivyasanarasikās+sundarīṇām+samūhās+|
krīḍāvāpyas+pratanusalilās+mālatīdāma rātris+
styānajyotsnā mudam+aviratam+kurvate yatra yūnām|| 42
body.translated_text: The warmth swelling at the breast-region, the saffron body-ointments, the swings dear to women addicted to the pleasure of play, the pools of slender water, the <s>mālatī</s> (jasmine) garlands, the nights dense with moonlight — there, they unceasingly delight the young. || 42 ||

body.text:
bhrāmyantīnām+tamasi nibiḍe vallabhākāṅkṣiṇīnām+
lākṣārāgās+caraṇagalitās+paurasīmantinīnām|
raktāśokastabakalalitais+bālabhānos+mayūkhais+
na+ālakṣyante rajanivigame pauramārgeṣu yatra|| 43
body.translated_text: Where the lac-dye fallen from the feet of city women wandering in the dense darkness longing for their lovers, is indistinguishable at dawn on the city streets from the lovely rays of the young sun, beautiful with clusters of red <s>Aśoka</s> flowers. || 43 ||

body.text:
ratnais+muktāmarakatamahānīlasaugandhikādyais+
śaṅkais+bālāvalayaracanābandhubhis+vidrumais+ca|
lopāmudrāramaṇamuninā pītaniḥśeṣavāras+
śrīḥsarvasvam+harati vipadam+yatra ratnākarasya|| 44
body.translated_text: Where, with gems — pearls, emeralds, great sapphires, fragrant stones, and corals (kindred of young women's bracelet-making) and conches — the ocean's entire wealth and calamity is seized, its waters entirely drunk by the husband-sage of <s>Lopāmudrā</s> (<s>Agastya</s>). || 44 ||

body.text:
mūkībhūtām+marakatamayīm+hārayaṣṭim+dadhānās+
yasmin+bālās+mṛgamadamasīpicchileṣu staneṣu|
cetovartismarahutavaham+dīpitam+snehapūrais+
kṛtvā yānti priyatamagṛhān+andhakāre ghane+api|| 45
body.translated_text: Where young women, wearing upon their breasts — slippery with musk and dark collyrium — a string of emerald beads rendered mute [by their beauty], having lit the fire of <s>Smara</s> (the god of love) as a lamp upon the wick of the heart, filled with the oil of affection, go to the homes of their most beloved, even in the densest darkness. || 45 ||

body.text:
nītam+yatnāt+avinayalipes+patratām+āyatākṣyā
nirgacchantyas+sapadi hṛdayam+kṣālayitvā+iva yatra|
kānte pādapraṇayini milatkajjalaśyāmalānām+
unmucyante nayanapayasām+śreṇayas+māninībhis+|| 46
body.translated_text: Where the leaf-letter, carefully composed by the long-eyed woman as a record of her beloved's misdeeds, as it departs instantly washes clean the heart, as it were, and from the proud women streams of tears, dark with commingled collyrium (<s>kajjala</s>), are released upon the beloved who bows at their feet in affection. || 46

body.text:
agre teṣām+vyapagatamadas+sthātum+eva+asamarthas+
dṛṣṭvā kāntim+kusumadhanuṣas+kā kathā vikramasya|
subhrūlīlācaturanayanakṣeparamyais+vilāsais+
yasmin+yātās+tat+api sudṛśām+kiṃkaratvam+yuvānas+|| 47
body.translated_text: Before those [women], even youths freed from intoxication are unable to stand still — upon seeing the beauty of the flower-bowed [god of love], what to speak of his valor! — where, by the charming glances cast with playfully arched, beautiful eyebrows, even young men have been reduced to servitude by those fair-eyed women. || 47

body.text:
tvayi+āsīni manasijagurau yatra sāraṅganetrās+
saṃdṛśyante racitacaturodyānadolāvilāsās+|
abhyasyantyas+sarabhasam+iva vyomakāntārayānam+
kandarpasya tridivayuvatīm+jetukāmasya senās+|| 48
body.translated_text: Where, when you are seated — O preceptor of the god of love — doe-eyed women are seen engaged in the delightful play of swings artfully arranged in pleasure-gardens, practicing, as it were, the vehement voyage through the sky — the armies of <s>Kandarpā</s> (the god of love) eager to conquer the celestial maidens. || 48

body.text:
prāsādānām+dinapariṇatau garbham+dagdhāgurūṇām+
jālodgīrṇas+sajalajaladaśyāmalas+yatra dhūmas+|
sadyaḥkrīḍākutukarabhasārūḍhapaurīmukhendujyotsnāsaṃgaprasṛmaratamaḥśreṇiśaṅkām+tanoti|| 49
body.translated_text: Where, at the day's end, from the interiors of mansions fragrant with burning <s>aguru</s> (aloe-wood), the smoke, dark as a rain-cloud laden with water, pouring forth through the latticed windows, creates the suspicion of spreading darkness clinging to the moonlight of the faces of the city-women who have eagerly ascended [the terraces] for their sudden sport. || 49

body.text:
vyarthībhūtapriyasahacarīcāruvācām+niśīthe
roṣāt+astrīkṛtakuvalayottaṃsavisraṃsimālyam|
yūnām+yatra praṇayakalaham+keliharmyāgrabhājām+
indus+pratyādiśati savidhībhūya śaśvat+kareṇa|| 50
body.translated_text: Where at midnight, the moon, approaching closely, constantly witnesses with its rays the love-quarrel of young men dwelling on the upper terraces of pleasure-palaces — their garlands of flowers tumbled and loosened from the <s>kuvalaya</s> (blue lotus) ear-ornaments thrown in anger, the sweet words of their beloved companions rendered fruitless by the quarrel. || 50

body.text:
tatra svecchārativinimaye ca+eav sīmantinīnām+
karṇasraṃsi prakṛtisubhagam+ketakīgarbhapatram|
utpaśyanti vyatikaracalatkuṇḍalāghaṭṭanābhis+
bhinnam+sākṣāt+iva mukhavidhos+khaṇḍam+ekam+vidagdhās+|| 51
body.translated_text: There, in the mutual exchange of pleasures at will among the married women, when the naturally lovely inner petal of the <s>ketakī</s> (screw-pine) flower slips from the ear, the connoisseurs, seeing [the reflection] moving with the clash of swinging earrings, behold what appears to be a single fragment of the face-moon itself. || 51

body.text:
vācas+śrotrāmṛtam+anugatabhrūvilāsās+kaṭākṣās+
rūpam+hastoccayasamucitam+snigdhamugdhās+ca hāvās+|
yātam+līlāñcitam+akṛtakam+yatra nepathyam+etat+
paurastrīṇām+draviṇasulabhā prakriyā bhūṣaṇam+ca|| 52
body.translated_text: Words that are nectar to the ears, sidelong glances accompanied by the play of eyebrows, beauty befitting the gathering of [embracing] arms, tender and innocent allurements, a gait that is naturally graceful and unaffected — this is the costume, and wealth easily obtained is the means, and ornaments the final touch — such is the way of the city-women there. || 52

body.text:
puñjībhūtam+jagat+iva tatas+saptakakṣyāniveśais+
ramyam+yāyās+bhavanam+avanīmaṇḍalākhaṇḍalasya|
yatsaudhānām+śikharisuhṛdām+mūrdhni viśrāntameghe
vidyullekhā vitarati muhus+vaijayantīvilāsam|| 53
body.translated_text: Then, from there, proceed to the beautiful palace of the lord of the earth's circle [the king], [a palace] like the entire world gathered into one, with its seven enclosures; on whose palace-pinnacles — those friends of the mountain-peaks — when a cloud has come to rest, the lightning-streak repeatedly creates the spectacle of a victory-banner (<s>vaijayantī</s>). || 53

body.text:
snigdhaśyāmais+iva viracitā dāritais+indranīlais+
vyāpī tasmin+avanivanitāramyaromāvalī+iva|
yasyās+tīre viharadanatiprauḍhasīmantinīnām+
manye līlāgatiṣu guravas+rājahaṃsās+bhavanti|| 54
body.translated_text: As if fashioned from split dark sapphires (<s>indranīla</s>), lustrous and dark, there spreads — like the charming line of body-hair of the Earth-maiden — [a river]; on whose banks, I think, the royal swans (<s>rājahaṃsa</s>) become teachers in the art of graceful gait to the not-yet-fully-matured young women who stroll about. || 54

body.text:
devam+sākṣāt+manasijam+iva prāptarājyābhiṣekam+
sevethās+tvam+vyathitasamaye cāmaragrāhiṇībhis+|
yasya snigdhasphuradasilatāsphāragatyā jalānām+
labdhas+sakhye ripukulavadhūlocanais+saṃvibhāgas+|| 55
body.translated_text: You should attend upon the king — [who is] like the visible god of love (<s>Manasija</s>) himself, having obtained the royal consecration — at the time of [the Gandharva maiden's] distress, [surrounded] by fan-bearing attendant women; whose [the king's] sword-blade flashes and flows with gleaming moisture, and in the [reflection of] whose friendship the eyes of the enemy's wives have obtained a share. || 55

body.text:
yasya+autsukyāt+asamasamarālokanonmādabhājām+
svargastrīṇām+aparigaṇitasrastacelāñcalānām|
manye dhārācaturaturagotkhātareṇupratānas+
sadyolagnas+stanakalaśayos+antarīyatvam+eti|| 56
body.translated_text: By whose [the king's] eagerness — for the enemy-wives maddened by the sight of his matchless combat, heedless of their upper garments' hems slipping down — I think the streams of dust raised by the swift hooves of [his] horses, instantly adhering [to their bodies], assume the role of an undergarment upon their pitcher-like breasts. || 56

body.text:
bhugnagrīvam+bhujabisalatāsaktavaktrāmbujābhis+
sas+ayam+senānvayanṛpas+iti trāsakautūhalābhyām|
viṣvak+pītas+kuvalayadalaśreṇidīrghais+kaṭākṣais+
paurastrībhis+sapadi nagarīvidrave vidviṣām+yas+|| 57
body.translated_text: He, this king of the <s>Sena</s> dynasty of army-commanders — whose neck bends [under the embrace], whose lotus-face is clasped by the vine-like arms of women — when the enemy city was being routed, was instantly drunk in on all sides by the long sidelong glances, [stretching like] rows of <s>kuvalaya</s> (blue lotus) petals, of the city's women, [gazing] with both fear and curiosity [wondering] 'This is he!' || 57

body.text:
baddhākrāndās+vihagaruditais+bibhratī caitasī+iva
krīḍāgāre suciralikhitām+ākṛtim+vallabhasya|
prauḍhārāmā yadarinagarī saudhasaṃjātadūrvājālavyājāt+alakapaṭalīm+dūranamrām+bibharti|| 58
body.translated_text: The enemy's fortified city, its cries of lamentation mingled with the wailing of birds, bearing in its pleasure-chamber, as it were, the mental image of the long-painted portrait of its lord — that mature city, like a woman, wears from the growth of grass upon its palace-walls, under the pretext of <s>dūrvā</s> (sacred grass) sprouts, a bowed and disheveled mass of hair in mourning. || 58

body.text:
krīḍāroṣe sutanucaraṇāhanyamānasya patyus+
pratyudgacchatpulakapaṭalena+api bādhām+dadhānā|
bhrāmyasi+adres+vanabhuvi katham+krūradarbhāṅkurāyām+
evaṃprāyas+yadarinagarīśārikāṇām+vilāpas+|| 59
body.translated_text: 'How do you wander on the forest-ground of this mountain, cruel with shoots of <s>darbha</s> grass — you who suffer pain even from the tingling wave of goosebumps when your husband's [feet], playfully struck by the delicate feet [of his beloved], rise in love's mock-anger?' — such is the nature of the laments of the <s>śārikā</s> (myna) birds of the enemy city. || 59

body.text:
tasmin+kāle kvacit+api sa cet+vāsarasya tribhāgam+
rājā śaktas+gamayati rahas+cintayan+antarāyān|
saṃdeśas+me na pavana tadā kiṃcit+āvedanīyas+
kāryottapte manasi labhate na+avakāśam+vilāsas+|| 60
body.translated_text: If at that time the king should happen to spend even a third part of the day in solitude, thinking of obstacles [to his plans], then, O wind, my message is not at all to be delivered — for when the mind is heated by pressing affairs, playful matters find no place. || 60

body.text:
āsādya+atas+kam+api samayam+saumya vaktum+vivikte
devam+nīcais+vinayacaturas+kāmin+prakramethās+|
api+anyeṣu praṇayibhis+abhivyañjitas+kāryabhāgas+
siddhim+gantum+prabhus+avasare kim+punas+pārthiveṣu|| 61
body.translated_text: Having approached [the king], at some opportune moment, O gentle one, you should begin to speak to the lord softly in private, skillful in courtesy, like a lover. For one whose purpose has been made known through intimates is capable of achieving success at the right moment — how much more so before kings! || 61

body.text:
śrīkhaṇḍādres+vasati śikhare kas+api gandharvalokas+
tatra+asti+ekā kuvalayavatī nāma mānyā+aṅganānām|
dūtam+tasyās+kalaya malayopatyakāmārutam+mām+
kāmidvandvam+ghaṭayati mithas+viprayuktam+yas+ekas+|| 62
body.translated_text: On the summit of Mount <s>Śrīkhaṇḍa</s> (Sandalwood Mountain) there dwells a certain <s>Gandharva</s> world. There lives one named <s>Kuvalayavatī</s>, revered among women. Regard me, the <s>Malaya</s> foothill breeze, as her messenger — I who am the one that unites a separated pair of lovers. || 62

body.text:
jitvā deva tvayi sarabhasam+dākṣiṇātyān+kṣitīśān+
pratyāvṛtte malayakaṭakāt+cittam+ādāya tasyās+|
dūram+yāte kamitari vṛthā vṛttis+asya+iti tasyās+
bāṣpotpīḍā sapadi padavīm+saṃrurodha+īkṣaṇasya|| 63
body.translated_text: O lord, when you returned impetuously from the <s>Malaya</s> range after conquering the southern kings, having carried away the heart of that [maiden] — when her beloved had gone far away, [she thought:] 'His existence is in vain.' Instantly, a flood of tears blocked the path of her eyes. || 63

body.text:
vinyasya+agram+bhuvi caraṇayos+kautukottambhitākṣī
tvatsamparkaprakṛtisubhagām+unnatagrīvam+āśām|
utpaśyantī kim+api sutanus+lakṣyate saudhaśṛṅgāt+
udbhinnāśrusthagitam+asakṛt+tvatsamīpam+yiyāsus+|| 64
body.translated_text: Placing the tips of her toes on the ground, with eyes raised in eager curiosity, she gazes with uplifted neck at the direction made beautiful by association with you. That slender girl is seen from the palace tower, wishing to come near you again and again, [her vision] obstructed by sprouting tears. || 64

body.text:
yasmin+kāle nayanaviṣayam+sāhasiniyā+asi nītas+
sāraṅgākṣyās+sakalalalanālocanānandakārin|
jāne tasmāt+prabhṛti janitasvāntasaṃtāpakhedā
sā ramyeṣu kvacit+api na viśvāsam+ekāntam+eti|| 65
body.translated_text: At the time when you, O bold one, were brought within the range of the eyes of that doe-eyed maiden, bringing delight to the eyes of all women — I know that from that moment, she who has suffered anguish from the heat generated in her heart does not fully trust anything pleasant, anywhere, at all. || 65

body.text:
muṣṭigrāhyam+kim+api vidhinā kurvatā madhyabhāgam+
manye bālā kusumadhanuṣas+nirmitā kārmukāya|
rājan+uccais+virahajanitakṣāmabhāvam+vahantī
jātā samprati+aha sutanus+sā ca maurvī latā+iva|| 66
body.translated_text: I think that young girl was fashioned by the Creator — who made her waist graspable in a fist — as a bowstring for the flower-bow [of <s>Kāma</s>]. O king, bearing an emaciated condition born of separation, she has now become indeed like a bowstring-vine, that slender one. || 66

body.text:
kīdṛk+kāntas+kathaya tarale vartate yas+tava+antar+
yatnāt+ittham+subhaga bahuśas+pṛṣṭayā+ālījanena|
niḥśvasya+uccais+katham+api tayā stambhitāśrupravāhā
nyastā dṛṣṭis+likhitamadane bhittibhāge gṛhasya|| 67
body.translated_text: 'Tell me, what is your beloved like, who dwells within your restless [heart]?' — thus repeatedly questioned with effort, O fortunate one, by her group of companions, having sighed deeply, somehow restraining the flow of tears, she cast her gaze upon the wall-panel of the house where the god of love was painted. || 67

body.text:
dhatte sadyas+tvadupagamitapremalekhabhramam+sā
tālīpatre priyasahacarīkarṇapāśacyute+api|
kim+ca krīḍāśukam+api muhus+pṛcchati tvatpravṛttim+
gāḍhodbhūtas+kva khalu gaṇayati+anvayam+tu+arthibhāvas+|| 68
body.translated_text: She immediately mistakes even a palm-leaf, fallen from the ear-ornament of a dear companion, for a love-letter brought by you. Moreover, she repeatedly asks even her pet parrot about news of you — for when longing has arisen deeply, who indeed considers proper sequence? || 68

body.text:
na+uttaṃsatvam+dṛśam+api nayati+utpale baddhakopā
mālyais+klāntā na bhujalatikām+api+asau saṃvṛṇoti|
padmodvignās+hṛdayanihitāt+tāpasampattihetos+
ālīhastāt+api ca sahasā mīlitākṣī bibheti|| 69
body.translated_text: In bound anger, she does not even bring a blue lotus (<s>utpala</s>) near her eyes as an ear-ornament. Weary of garlands, she does not cover even her arm-vine [with them]. Alarmed by lotuses (<s>padma</s>) — because of the wealth of heat placed in her heart — she even shrinks with closed eyes from the hand of a companion. || 69

body.text:
abhyasyantī sarasakusumasvastaros+prāntasuptā
śuṣyatpaṅkaprakarasapharīsambhramodvartitāni|
dhārābāṣpam+nayananalinīnālatām+ca+ānayantī
manye bālā gamayati punas+sā kathaṃcit+dināni|| 70
body.translated_text: I think that young girl somehow passes her days — sleeping at the edge of a bed spread with fresh, moist flowers, [and] bringing about a state of tears flowing like streams and a creeper-like condition of her lotus-eyes, [resembling] the floundering of fish in drying mud-pools. || 70

body.text:
antas+tāpam+tuhinapayasām+api+anucchidyam+āpya
tvattas+bālās+malayajarajaḥsrotasām+api+asādhyam|
dhatte nindām+kusumaviśikhe+atyantasādṛśyamūḍhā
susthā+api syāt+kim+uta virahavyākulās+vibhramiṇyas+|| 71
body.translated_text: Having acquired an inner heat that is not extinguished even by cool waters, and that — originating from you, O [king] — is incurable even by streams of <s>Malaya</s> sandalwood paste, she, deluded by [the fire of separation's] extreme resemblance [to Kāma's arrows], hurls reproaches at the flower-arrowed [god of love]. Even a healthy woman would be confused — how much more so one distracted by separation! || 71

body.text:
dveṣas+krīḍāvipinavasatau candanāmbhoniṣedhas+
pratyākhyānam+sarasanalinītālavṛntānilasya|
jātas+tasyām+katham+api sakhībuddhijas+tvadviyoge
mūrchāvegavyapagamavidhes+eṣas+eva prakāras+|| 72
body.translated_text: Aversion to the pleasure-garden dwelling, prohibition of sandalwood water, rejection of the breeze from lotus-leaf fans — this is the only method, devised somehow through the wisdom of her companions, for dispelling the intensity of her fainting spells during separation from you. || 72

body.text:
dhatte dveṣam+śaśini kurute na graham+keśahaste
dūre hāram+kṣipati ramate nindayā candanasya|
vaktum+deva tvayi param+asau svām+avasthām+kathaṃcit+
gāḍhodvegā nayati kavitācintayā vāsarāṇi|| 73
body.translated_text: She bears resentment toward the moon, does not accept her companion's hand in her hair, casts her necklace far away, and amuses herself with reproaches of sandalwood. O lord, to somehow express her condition to you, that deeply agitated girl passes her days absorbed in poetic composition. || 73

body.text:
ādau yātas+nayanapadavīm+stambhayan+pakṣmamālām+
cumban+gaṇḍasthalabhuvam+atho pītabimbādharoṣṭhas+|
kurvan+kaṇṭhagraham+api kucotsaṅgaśayyāśayānas+
tasyās+bāṣpas+kim+iva na khalu tvadviyoge karoti|| 74
body.translated_text: At first entering the path of her eyes, arresting the row of eyelashes, kissing the surface of her cheeks, then sipping from her <s>bimba</s>-red lower lip, embracing her neck, reclining on the bed of her bosom — what indeed does her tear not do in separation from you! || 74

body.text:
śāraṅgākṣyā janayati na yat+bhasmasāt+aṅgakāni
tvadviśleṣe smarahutavahas+śvāsasaṃdhukṣitas+api|
jāne tasyās+sa khalu nayanadroṇivārām+prabhāvas+
yat+vā śaśvat+nṛpa tava manovartinas+śītalasya|| 75
body.translated_text: That the fire of <s>Smara</s> (love), though fanned by her sighs, does not reduce the limbs of that doe-eyed maiden to ashes in separation from you — I know that this is surely the power of the waters from the vessels of her eyes; or perhaps, O king, it is [the power] of the coolness of [the thought of] you that dwells in her mind. || 75

body.text:
śāntaprāye rajanisamaye kiṃcit+āmīlitākṣī
prāpya svapne katham+api puras+tvām+atiprauḍharāgā|
śliṣyantī svām+tanum+anupadam+viprabuddhā+atha bālā
lajjālolam+balayati mukham+sā sakhīnām+mukheṣu|| 76
body.translated_text: When the night-watch is nearly spent, the young girl, her eyes slightly closed, having somehow reached you in a dream, intensely passionate, embraces her own body. Then, suddenly awakened, she bashfully turns her face away among the faces of her companions. // 76

body.text:
candrāt+ramyām+upavanabhuvam+dūratas+dveṣṭi bālā
na+ālāpam+ca kvacana kurute sārdham+ālījanena|
rakṣāhetos+smaraviśikhatas+kevalam+sā varākī
dhatte līlāphalakam+urasi tvatpraticchandaśobhi|| 77
body.translated_text: The girl despises the pleasure-garden ground made lovely by the moonlight from afar, nor does she anywhere engage in conversation with her circle of companions. Merely for protection against the arrows of <s>Smara</s> (the god of love), the hapless girl holds upon her breast a toy shield (<s>līlāphalaka</s>) that shines with your reflected image. // 77

body.text:
vinyasyantī śaśini nayane durdinais+aśruvārām+
dhārāśvāsais+bakulakusumāmodam+āghrātukāmā|
śuśrūṣas+ca bhramaravirutam+mūrchayā rakṣitā+asau
vīkṣya+avasthām+kas+iva karuṇākātaras+syāt+na tasyās+|| 78
body.translated_text: Casting upon the moon her eyes — [streams] of tears [caused] by gloomy days — desirous of smelling the fragrance of <s>bakula</s> flowers through the respite of rain-showers, and wishing to listen to the humming of bees — she is restrained by fainting. Who indeed, seeing her condition, would not be overcome with compassion? // 78

body.text:
cetovṛttis+sphurati karuṇā viprayoge virāgas+
kopāveśas+kusumaviśikhe nityam+ātmani+avajñā|
ittham+svāṅge sthitam+iva samālambya citrā varākī
tvayi+ekāntasthiraviracitam+bhāvam+āviṣkaroti|| 79
body.translated_text: Her mind's activity flickers; there is compassion [in some], in separation there is detachment; there is fury toward the flower-arrowed one [<s>Kāma</s>]; there is constant self-reproach. Thus the hapless girl, clinging as it were to the manifold [emotions] stationed in her own body, reveals her love that is steadfastly and exclusively fixed upon you. // 79

body.text:
prāk+ālāpās+pratimuhus+api premaramyās+sakhīnās+
tvaji+ekāntavyapagatadaye saṃgamāśā+api na+eva|
tasyās+cintām+virahajanitām+nātha vismārayantī
mūrchā+eva+ekā bhavati satatam+jīvitālambanāya|| 80
body.translated_text: The conversations of her companions, formerly delightful with love at every turn — since you have become exclusively indifferent, there is not even hope of union. O lord, the only thing that constantly serves as a lifeline for her is fainting itself, which makes her forget the grief born of separation. // 80

body.text:
tasyās+rājan+anubhavam+anāsādyahastāvarodhāt+
gaṇḍābhoge nayanasalilasrotasā kṣālitas+api|
pratyāsannas+stanaparisare cetasā tvām+vahantyās+
prāleyāṃśus+nṛpatikakudacchatrabhaṅgīm+bibharti|| 81
body.translated_text: O king, the moon — upon the surface of her cheeks, washed by the stream of tears from her eyes, yet unattainable by the embrace of your hand — and near the vicinity of her breasts as she carries you in her heart — bears the semblance of a broken royal parasol. // 81

body.text:
yātas+kṛcchrāt+tuhinasamayas+samprati tvatsakāśāt+
āgacchantīm+pavanalaharīm+api+anāsādayantyās+|
kas+sannaddhe parabhṛtavadhūkelivācālalole
caitre tasyās+kathaya subhaga prāṇarakṣābhyupāyas+|| 82
body.translated_text: The cold season has barely passed; and now, for her who cannot even encounter a wave of wind coming from your direction, when the aggressive <s>Caitra</s> month arrives, noisy with the amorous cries of cuckoo-wives — tell me, O blessed one, what means will preserve her life? // 82

body.text:
bhūyas+bhūyas+praviśati manas+dāruṇe manmathāgnau
magnam+bāṣpāmbhasi nayanayos+dvandvam+indīvarākṣyās+|
tasyās+rājan+atanuvirahavyākulāyās+tapasvī
jātas+bhasmacchuritas+iva sa kṣāmapāṇḍus+kapolas+|| 83
body.translated_text: Again and again the mind of that lotus-eyed girl enters the terrible fire of <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love), while the pair of her eyes is submerged in tears. O king, her cheek, that of the wretched one intensely tormented by separation, has become pale and wan, as if dusted with ashes. // 83

body.text:
rājan+urvīvalayavanitākāmuka tvatsakāśāt+
āśātantus+bhavatu sudṛśas+durlabhas+prematantus+|
kaṣṭāt+kaṣṭam+punar+idam+aho svapnasaṃketadūtī
nidrā+api+asyās+kṣaṇam+api na yat+netrasīmānam+eti|| 84
body.translated_text: O king, lover of the women of the earth's circle, let there be from your presence a thread of hope for that beautiful-eyed girl — a rare thread of love! How grievous upon grievous it is that even sleep, the messenger who arranges dream-trysts, does not reach the boundary of her eyes even for a moment! // 84

body.text:
pratyāvṛttās+stanaparisarāt+candanasphītamūrtes+
śvāsās+eva smarahutavahoddīpanaikapragalbhās+|
tām+utkaṇṭhākulitahṛdayām+khedayanti prakāmam+
samprāpyante malayapavanais+evam+eva+ayaśāṃsi|| 85
body.translated_text: The sighs returning from the vicinity of her breasts — thick with sandal paste — those very [sighs] that are singularly bold in fanning the fire of <s>Smara</s> (the god of love), torment her who is distressed with longing exceedingly. Thus do even the <s>Malaya</s> breezes gain dishonor. // 85

body.text:
tvadvaktrānusmaraṇarasikā kātarā ca prakāmam+
jyotsnāsekais+dvijapatim+adhikṣepapātram+karoti|
kim+ca dveṣṭi tridaśabhiṣajau sundara tvām+vicintya
prāyeṇa+evam+bhavati vidhurāsannamṛtyos+manīṣā|| 86
body.translated_text: Relishing the remembrance of your face, and exceedingly anxious, she reproaches the moon (<s>dvijapatim</s>) with [its] drenching moonlight. Moreover, O handsome one, thinking of you, she loathes even the physicians of the gods (<s>Aśvinīkumāras</s>). For generally the thoughts of one near death from love-sickness turn to such things. // 86

body.text:
sā vairasyāt+asitanayanā hematālīdalānām+
pratyākhyānāt+prakṛtisubhagam+karṇapāśam+bibharti|
tadgātrāṇām+kim+api sahasā durbalatvam+vicintya
tyaktam+trāsāt+guṇam+iva manojanmanā kārmukasya|| 87
body.translated_text: That dark-eyed girl, out of aversion to the golden palm-leaf [ear ornaments], having rejected them, wears her naturally beautiful ear-loops. Suddenly reflecting on some weakness of those [her] limbs, the flower-armed [god of love (<s>Manoja</s>)] has in fear abandoned the string of his bow, as it were. // 87

body.text:
api+ājanmaprabhṛtisuhṛdas+candanasya+aparādhāt+
adhyāste sā na khalu malayopatyakākānanāni|
kim+ca dveṣāt+upari madanasya+iva sarvāṅgatanvī
baddhāveśā manasi rataye na+avakāśam+dadāti|| 88
body.translated_text: Moreover, because of her offense against sandal paste — her companion since birth — she no longer frequents the forest-groves on the slopes of the <s>Malaya</s> mountain. And, as if out of hatred for <s>Madana</s> (the god of love), she whose entire body has become thin, firmly resolved in her mind, gives love (<s>rati</s>) no room. // 88

body.text:
līlodyāne vitarati dṛśam+yatnasaṃruddhabāṣpā
sāndre candrārciṣi niviśate candanābhyaktagātrī|
krīḍāvāpīm+marut+abhimukham+dhāvati vyākulā+asau
kim+vā nāryas+ramaṇavirahe sāhasam+na+ācaranti|| 89
body.translated_text: In the pleasure-garden she casts her gaze with tears forcibly held back. In the dense moonlight she settles down, her body anointed with sandal paste. Toward the pleasure-lake she runs agitated, facing the wind. For what acts of desperation do women not perform in separation from their beloved? // 89

body.text:
yātās+kaṇṭhasthalam+api ghanaśvāsamātrāvaśeṣās+
tām+utkaṇṭhāpratanum+asavas+sarvathā na tyajanti|
labdhvā kaṇṭhapraṇayam+athavā tādṛśam+aṅganānām+
śaktas+tyāge kas+iva bhuvane cetasā vicyutas+api|| 90
body.translated_text: Her life-breaths, which have reached her throat — with only dense sighing remaining — do not abandon that girl whose longing has become intense, by any means whatsoever. Or rather, having obtained the intimacy of such women's throats, who in the world, even if bereft of consciousness, is capable of abandonment? // 90

body.text:
kṣīṇas+tāpas+vapuṣi vigatā netrayos+aśrudhārā
viśrāntāni kramakṛśatanos+aṅgavikṣepaṇāni|
ittham+śānte virahajanite vyādhirāge mṛgākṣyās+
śvāsas+tasyās+param+upacitas+nirvṛtes+antarāyas+|| 91
body.translated_text: The burning in her body has diminished, the stream of tears from her eyes has ceased, the tossings of her limbs — emaciated step by step — have subsided; thus, though the fever of love born of separation has calmed in the doe-eyed one, her sighing is now intensified — an obstacle to her peace. || 91

body.text:
līlodyāne parabhṛtavadhūpañcamais+pīḍyamānā
tāmyanmūrtis+malayamarutā kelivātāyaneṣu|
sā na+ekatra kvacit+api padam+kātarākṣī vidhatte
yat+satyam+na tribhuvanam+api prītaye duḥkhitānām|| 92
body.translated_text: Tormented by the fifth notes of the female cuckoos in the pleasure-garden, her body wilting in the <s>Malaya</s> breezes [blowing through] the latticed pleasure-windows, that anxious-eyed girl finds no place to rest anywhere; for truly, not even the three worlds bring delight to those who are suffering. || 92

body.text:
sā sarvatra+apratihatagatis+vidyayā sati+api tvām+
pratyākhyānāt+subhaga sahasā bibhyatī na+abhyupaiti|
rājānas+hi prakṛtirasavaccetasas+api+anyanārīm+
rūḍhapremaprabalavanitābhīravas+no lasanti|| 93
body.translated_text: Though she possesses the magic power to go anywhere unobstructed, O handsome one, she does not come to you suddenly, fearing rejection; for kings, even though their hearts are naturally susceptible to passion, when intimidated by the strength of love for their established beloved, do not dally with another woman. || 93

body.text:
tasyās+tīvrasmarahutabhujā dahyamānāṅgayaṣṭes+
nyastam+sadyas+stanaparisare candanam+śoṣam+eti|
uktais+kim+vā bahubhis+apadāropitasvāntavṛttes+
tvayi+āyattas+kuvalayadṛśas+jīvarakṣāprakāras+|| 94
body.translated_text: Of her whose body-staff is being consumed by the fierce fire of <s>Smara</s> (the god of love), the sandalwood paste freshly applied to the region of her breasts instantly dries up. But what use are many words? The means of preserving the life of the lotus-eyed one depends on you — you, from whom her heart's devotion has never been removed. || 94

body.text:
iti+ākhyāte pulakitatanus+medinīpuṣpaketus+
pratyutthāya praṇayasubhagam+gāḍham+āśliṣyati tvām|
vākyais+ebhis+karuṇamasṛṇais+komalatvam+bhajante
grāvāṇas+api prakṛtisarasas+kim+punas+tādṛśas+yas+|| 95
body.translated_text: When [the message] has been thus told, the <s>Medinīpuṣpaketu</s> (the king, "banner of the earth's flowers"), his body thrilling with goosebumps, will rise and tightly embrace you with deep affection. By these words, tender with compassion, even stones become soft — how much more one such as he, who is naturally full of feeling! || 95

body.text:
sadyas+kṛtvā pavana vinayāt+añjalim+mūrdhni kiṃcit+
vaktavyas+asau rahasi bhavatā madgirā gauḍarājas+|
tvattas+śroṣyati+avahitamanās+sas+anuraktāṅganānām+
jāyante hi praṇayini sudhāvīcayas+vācikāni|| 96
body.translated_text: O wind, immediately placing your palms together upon your head with a bow of respect, you must address that <s>Gauḍa</s> king privately on my behalf; he will listen with attentive mind — for in the words of loving women, there arise waves of nectar. || 96

body.text:
pārśve paścāt+api ca puratas+darśayan+ātmarūpam+
vyaktam+deva tvam+asi jagatām+īśvaras+śārṅgapāṇis+|
tat+mām+bhaktipravaṇamanasam+na+anugṛhṇāsi kasmāt+
kāyavyūham+racayitum+alam+na+aparas+kaiṭabhāres+|| 97
body.translated_text: "Displaying your own form at the side, behind, and before [you] — O lord, you are clearly the <s>Śārṅgapāṇi</s> (Wielder of the Bow, i.e., <s>Viṣṇu</s>), the Lord of the worlds. Then why do you not favor me, whose mind is inclined toward devotion? No one other than the destroyer of <s>Kaiṭabha</s> [<s>Viṣṇu</s>] is capable of multiplying his bodily forms. || 97

body.text:
saudhotsaṅge mukulitadṛśam+tatsakhīnām+purastāt+
mām+āsādya tvam+ayam+akṛthās+gocare yat+na vācām|
tat+kurvīthās+subhaga na satām+garhaṇīyā yathā syām+
kanyām+loke na khalu sudhiyas+dūṣayitvā tyajanti|| 98
body.translated_text: Having approached me as I sat with half-closed eyes in the lap of the palace, before her friends, you made me — this one — enter a state beyond the reach of words. Therefore, O handsome one, do such a thing that I may not become a target of reproach among the virtuous — for the wise do not indeed dishonor and then abandon a maiden in this world." || 98

body.text:
vṛtte gaurīpariṇayavidhau pīvaraprītibhājā
sṛṣṭasya+iva tripurajayinā puṣpaketis+navasya|
rājan+astu praṇayacaturas+dūratas+premabandhas+
puṇyena syām+tava caraṇayos+kena saṃvāhane+api|| 99
body.translated_text: "O king, when the rite of <s>Gaurī</s>'s (Pārvatī's) marriage was performed, you were like a newly created <s>Puṣpaketu</s> (god of love), fashioned by the conqueror of <s>Tripura</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) with overflowing delight. Let the bond of love, skilled in affection, extend far — by some merit may I serve even at the washing of your feet!" || 99

body.text:
saṃdeśas+ayam+manasi nihitas+kaccit+āyuṣmatā me
kim+vā bhūyas+tvayi viracitais+aṅga bhikṣāprakārais+|
pārārthyaikapravaṇamanasas+tvadvidhās+bāṣpamiśrān+
āpannānām+na khalu bahuśas+kākuvādān+sahante|| 100
body.translated_text: "Has this message been kept in mind by the long-lived one? Or have I importuned you further, O dear one, with these many modes of entreaty? Those like you, whose minds are solely inclined toward the welfare of others, cannot bear to hear the tearful, plaintive words of the afflicted many times." || 100

body.text:
dantivyūham+kanakalatikām+cāmaram+haimadaṇḍam+
yas+gauḍendrāt+alabhata kavikṣmābhṛtām+cakravartī|
śrīdhoyīkas+sakalarasikaprītihetos+manasvī
kāvyam+sārasvatam+iva mahāmantram+etat+jagāda|| 101
body.translated_text: He who obtained from the lord of <s>Gauḍa</s> the array of elephants, a golden vine-ornament, a <s>cāmara</s> (fly-whisk), and a golden-handled [parasol] — the sovereign among poet-kings, the spirited <s>Śrī Dhoyīka</s>, composed this poem for the delight of all connoisseurs, like a great mantra of <s>Sarasvatī</s>. || 101

body.text:
goṣṭhībandhas+sakalakavibhis+vāci vaidarbharītis+
vāsas+gaṅgāparisarabhuvi snigdhabhogyā vibhūtis+|
satsu snehas+sadasi kavitācāryakam+bhūbhujām+me
bhaktis+lakṣmīpaticaraṇayos+astu janmāntare+api|| 102
body.translated_text: May there be for me, even in the next birth: fellowship with all poets, the <s>Vaidarbha</s> style in speech, residence on the banks of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, wealth of pleasing enjoyments, affection among the good, the mastery of poetry in assemblies, and devotion at the feet of <s>Lakṣmīpati</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>). || 102

body.text:
yāvat+śambhus+vahati girijāsaṃvibhaktam+śarīram+
yāvat+jaitram+kalayati dhanus+kausumam+puṣpaketus+|
yāvat+rādhāramaṇataruṇīkelisākṣī kadambas+
tāvat+jīyāt+kavinarapates+eṣa vācām+vilāsas+|| 103
body.translated_text: As long as <s>Śambhu</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) bears his body shared with <s>Girijā</s> (<s>Pārvatī</s>), as long as <s>Puṣpaketu</s> (the god of love) wields his victorious bow of flowers, as long as the <s>kadamba</s> tree is witness to the sports of the beloved of <s>Rādhā</s>'s lord [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] — so long may this verbal delight of the king of poets be victorious! || 103

body.text:
kīrtis+labdhā sadasi viduṣām+śītalakṣoṇipālās+
vāksaṃdarbhās+katicit+amṛtasyandinas+nirmitās+ca|
tīre samprati+amarasaritas+kva+api śailopakaṇṭhe
brahmābhyāse prayatamanasā netum+īhe dināni|| 104
body.translated_text: Fame has been won in the assembly of the learned; a few literary compositions dripping with nectar have been created. Now, on the bank of the celestial river [<s>Gaṅgā</s>], somewhere in the vicinity of the mountains, I wish to spend my days with concentrated mind in the practice of the study of <s>Brahman</s>. || 104

body.text: śrīdhoyīkavirājaviracitam+pavanadūtākhyam+kāvyam+samāptam|
body.translated_text: Thus ends the poem called <s>Pavanadūta</s> (The Wind Messenger), composed by the poet <s>Śrī Dhoyīka</s>.
